newsitem.title: USA: Paris Club sees new debt terms as soon as possible.
newsitem.headline: Paris Club sees new debt terms as soon as possible.

text.p: The Paris Club of creditor nations plans to provide new terms of debt relief on a case-by-case basis as soon as possible, a source close to the Paris Club chairmanship said on Saturday.
The Paris Club has agreed to offer debt relief of up to 80 percent to poor nations compared to 67 percent currently available under Naples terms of debt relief, the source said.

The source said he could not say which country would be the first to benefit from the new terms, which France has dubbed Lyon terms after a Group of Seven summit in Lyon, France in June which called for improved debt relief.

Countries seeking debt relief of up to 80 percent will have to conclude a new agreement on economic reforms with the International Monetary Fund (IMF). Paris Club debt accords traditionally follow an IMF agreement.

The Paris Club source stressed that individual debtor countries had each very different needs in terms of debt relief. The new terms "will be put into practice on a case-by-case basis. The sooner the better," he said.
